seo.description: 20 High-yield JEE Main MCQ practice questions covering centripetal acceleration, conical pendulum, level & banked road skidding thresholds, death well dynamics, overturning criteria, rotating liquid surfaces, and connected radial masses.

conceptCapsule.title: Centripetal Acceleration, Radial Equilibrium & Real-World Applications
conceptCapsule.summary: 1. Kinematics of UCM: In uniform circular motion with constant speed $v$, tangential acceleration is zero ($a_t = 0$), and purely radial centripetal acceleration operates: $a_c = \frac{v^2}{R} = \omega^2 R$. The net work done by centripetal force is always zero. 2. Conical Pendulum: Tension resolves as $T\cos\theta = mg$ and $T\sin\theta = m\omega^2 (L\sin\theta)$, yielding $T_p = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L\cos\theta}{g}}$. 3. Road Vehicles: Safe speed on a flat rough road is $v \le \sqrt{\mu_s R g}$. On a friction-free banked road, optimum speed is $v_0 = \sqrt{Rg\tan\theta}$. With friction, the safe speed envelope is $\sqrt{Rg\left[\frac{\tan\theta - \mu_s}{1 + \mu_s\tan\theta}\right]} \le v \le \sqrt{Rg\left[\frac{\tan\theta + \mu_s}{1 - \mu_s\tan\theta}\right]}$. 4. Rotor / Death Well: Normal reaction provides centripetal force ($N = \frac{mv^2}{R}$), and static friction balances weight ($f_s = mg \le \mu_s N$), requiring $v_{\text{min}} = \sqrt{\frac{Rg}{\mu_s}}$. 5. Vehicle Overturning: To prevent toppling before skidding on an unbanked curve with wheel base $2d$ and center of mass height $h$, $v_{\text{topple}} = \sqrt{\frac{Rgd}{h}}$.
conceptCapsule.examTrap: Remember that centripetal force is NOT a separate physical fundamental force like gravity or tension. It is merely the net inward radial resultant force ($\sum F_{\text{radial}} = \frac{mv^2}{R}$) provided by real physical agencies such as string tension, normal reaction, friction, or gravity.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m$ moves in a horizontal circular path of radius $R$ with a constant speed $v$. The magnitude of the average acceleration over a quarter of a revolution is:
questions.solution:
1. Change in velocity vector: $|\Delta\vec{v}| = |(-v\hat{i}) - (v\hat{j})| = \sqrt{v^2 + v^2} = \sqrt{2}v$.
2. Time taken: $\Delta t = \frac{(\pi/2)R}{v} = \frac{\pi R}{2v}$.
3. Average acceleration: $a_{\text{avg}} = \frac{|\Delta\vec{v}|}{\Delta t} = \frac{\sqrt{2}v}{\frac{\pi R}{2v}} = \frac{2\sqrt{2}v^2}{\pi R}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A conical pendulum consists of a bob of mass $m$ attached to a light string of length $L$ rotating in a horizontal circle of radius $r$. If the string makes an angle $\theta$ with the vertical, the time period of revolution is:
questions.solution:
Vertical balance: $T\cos\theta = mg$. Horizontal balance: $T\sin\theta = m\omega^2(L\sin\theta) \implies \omega = \sqrt{\frac{g}{L\cos\theta}}$.
Time period: $T_p = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L\cos\theta}{g}}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A car travels along a level circular road of radius $R = 50\text{ m}$. If the coefficient of static friction between the tyres and the road is $\mu_s = 0.5$, the maximum safe speed without skidding is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
$$v_{\text{max}} = \sqrt{\mu_s R g} = \sqrt{0.5 \times 50 \times 10} = \sqrt{250} \approx 15.81\text{ m/s}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A curved track of radius $R$ is banked at an angle $\theta$. The optimum speed $v_0$ at which a vehicle can round the curve without relying on friction between tyres and the road is:
questions.solution:
Normal force components: $N\sin\theta = \frac{mv_0^2}{R}$ and $N\cos\theta = mg$.
Dividing: $\tan\theta = \frac{v_0^2}{Rg} \implies v_0 = \sqrt{Rg\tan\theta}$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A motorcyclist loops inside a cylindrical vertical rotor ('Death Well') of radius $R = 4\text{ m}$. If the coefficient of static friction between the wall and tyres is $\mu_s = 0.4$, the minimum horizontal circular speed needed to keep the rider from sliding down is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
1. Wall normal reaction provides centripetal force: $N = \frac{mv^2}{R}$.
2. Vertical equilibrium: $f_s = mg \le \mu_s N = \mu_s \frac{mv^2}{R} \implies v \ge \sqrt{\frac{Rg}{\mu_s}}$.
3. Minimum speed: $v_{\text{min}} = \sqrt{\frac{4 \times 10}{0.4}} = \sqrt{100} = 10\text{ m/s}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A small coin is placed at a distance $r = 10\text{ cm}$ from the center of a horizontal rotating turntable. If $\mu_s = 0.4$, the maximum frequency of rotation (in rev/min) for the coin not to slide off is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2, \pi^2 \approx 10$):
questions.solution:
1. $\omega_{\text{max}} = \sqrt{\frac{\mu_s g}{r}} = \sqrt{\frac{0.4 \times 10}{0.1}} = \sqrt{40}\text{ rad/s}$.
2. Frequency $f = \frac{\omega}{2\pi} = \frac{\sqrt{40}}{2\pi} \approx \frac{2\sqrt{10}}{2\sqrt{10}} = 1\text{ rev/s} = 60\text{ rpm}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: An aircraft executes a horizontal turn of radius $R = 1000\text{ m}$ at a uniform speed of $v = 200\text{ m/s}$. The angle of banking $\theta$ that the wings must make with the horizontal to prevent side-slipping is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
For coordinated flight: $\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{Rg} = \frac{200^2}{1000 \times 10} = \frac{40000}{10000} = 4 \implies \theta = \tan^{-1}(4)$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m$ is suspended from the ceiling of a railway carriage by a string of length $l$. If the train rounds a horizontal circular curve of radius $R$ with speed $v$, the tension in the string is:
questions.solution:
The string hangs along the direction of apparent gravity $\vec{g}_{\text{eff}} = \vec{g} - \vec{a}_c$.
Tension $T = m g_{\text{eff}} = m\sqrt{g^2 + a_c^2} = m\sqrt{g^2 + \frac{v^4}{R^2}}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: In a banked circular road of radius $R$, angle of banking $\theta$, and coefficient of friction $\mu_s < \tan\theta$, the minimum speed $v_{\text{min}}$ below which a vehicle tends to slip down the bank is:
questions.solution:
At minimum speed, friction acts uphill: $N\cos\theta + f\sin\theta = mg$ and $N\sin\theta - f\cos\theta = \frac{mv^2}{R}$.
Solving with $f = \mu_s N$ gives $v_{\text{min}} = \sqrt{Rg\left[\frac{\tan\theta - \mu_s}{1 + \mu_s\tan\theta}\right]}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A smooth hemispherical bowl of radius $R$ is rotated about its vertical axis of symmetry with angular speed $\omega$. A small particle placed on its inner surface stays in circular equilibrium at a depth $h$ below the rim ($h < R$). The angular velocity $\omega$ is:
questions.solution:
Let angle with vertical be $\theta$: $\cos\theta = \frac{R-h}{R}$ and circle radius $r = R\sin\theta$.
Equilibrium gives $N\cos\theta = mg$ and $N\sin\theta = m\omega^2 r = m\omega^2(R\sin\theta)$.
$$\frac{mg}{\cos\theta} = m\omega^2 R \implies \omega = \sqrt{\frac{g}{R\cos\theta}} = \sqrt{\frac{g}{R - h}}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A light string of length $L$ can withstand a maximum tension $T_{\text{max}} = 100\text{ N}$. A stone of mass $m = 0.5\text{ kg}$ is tied to it and whirled in a horizontal circle on a frictionless horizontal tabletop. The maximum speed the stone can have without breaking the string is ($L = 2\text{ m}$):
questions.solution:
$$T_{\text{max}} = \frac{m v_{\text{max}}^2}{L} \implies v_{\text{max}} = \sqrt{\frac{T_{\text{max}} L}{m}} = \sqrt{\frac{100 \times 2}{0.5}} = \sqrt{400} = 20.0\text{ m/s}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: Two identical bodies $A$ and $B$, each of mass $m$, are attached to a central pivot by two light strings of equal length $L$ along the same radial line and rotated on a smooth horizontal table at uniform angular speed $\omega$. The ratio of tension in string section $OA$ to string section $AB$ is:
questions.solution:
1. For outer mass $B$ (radius $2L$): $T_{AB} = m\omega^2(2L) = 2m\omega^2 L$.
2. For inner mass $A$ (radius $L$): $T_{OA} - T_{AB} = m\omega^2 L \implies T_{OA} = 2m\omega^2 L + m\omega^2 L = 3m\omega^2 L$.
3. Ratio: $\frac{T_{OA}}{T_{AB}} = \frac{3}{2}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A car rounds an unbanked circular curve of radius $R$ with speed $v$. The distance between its two inner and outer wheels is $2d$, and the height of its center of mass above the ground is $h$. The maximum speed to avoid overturning is:
questions.solution:
At the verge of overturning, normal force on the inner wheels vanishes ($N_{\text{inner}} = 0$).
Taking torque about CM: $(mg)d - \left(\frac{mv^2}{R}\right)h = 0 \implies v_{\text{max}} = \sqrt{\frac{Rgd}{h}}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: When a particle moves with uniform speed in a circle of radius $R$, the work done by the centripetal force over a half revolution is:
questions.solution:
Centripetal force is always perpendicular to the instantaneous velocity vector ($\vec{F}_c \cdot d\vec{r} = 0$). Thus, work done by the centripetal force is identically zero over any displacement.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A cyclist bends inwards while negotiating a sharp level horizontal curve of radius $R$ with speed $v$. The angle $\theta$ made by the cycle frame with the vertical is:
questions.solution:
The resultant reaction force passes through the center of gravity to provide zero net torque: $\tan\theta = \frac{f_s}{N} = \frac{mv^2/R}{mg} = \frac{v^2}{Rg} \implies \theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{v^2}{Rg}\right)$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A hollow vertical cone of semi-vertical angle $\alpha$ rotates about its axis with constant angular velocity $\omega$. A small block is in circular motion at distance $r$ from the axis on the smooth inner surface. The required angular velocity $\omega$ is:
questions.solution:
Normal force is inclined at $\alpha$ to the vertical: $N\sin\alpha = mg$ and $N\cos\alpha = m\omega^2 r$.
Dividing gives $\frac{1}{\tan\alpha} = \frac{\omega^2 r}{g} \implies \omega = \sqrt{\frac{g}{r\tan\alpha}}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A bead of mass $m$ is threaded on a smooth horizontal rod of length $L$ pivoted at one end. A spring of stiffness $k$ and natural length $l_0$ connects the bead to the pivot. If the rod rotates with constant angular speed $\omega < \sqrt{k/m}$, the stretch $x$ in the spring is:
questions.solution:
The spring tension provides the centripetal acceleration: $kx = m\omega^2(l_0 + x) \implies (k - m\omega^2)x = m\omega^2 l_0 \implies x = \frac{m\omega^2 l_0}{k - m\omega^2}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A railway engine of mass $M$ moves at speed $v$ along a curved track of radius $R$. The outer rail is raised above the inner rail by height $h$ (gauge separation $d$). For no lateral thrust on the rails:
questions.solution:
For small elevation angle: $\sin\theta \approx \tan\theta \implies \frac{h}{d} = \frac{v^2}{Rg} \implies h = \frac{v^2 d}{Rg}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: An open container filled with liquid of density $\rho$ is rotated at constant angular velocity $\omega$ about its central vertical axis. The shape of the free surface of the liquid is:
questions.solution:
Slope at radial coordinate $r$ is $\frac{dy}{dr} = \frac{\omega^2 r}{g} \implies y = \frac{\omega^2 r^2}{2g}$, representing a paraboloid of revolution.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A tube of length $L$ filled completely with an incompressible liquid of total mass $M$ is closed at both ends and rotated horizontally about one end with angular speed $\omega$. The force exerted by the liquid on the outer closed end is:
questions.solution:
Integrating centripetal force for all liquid elements: $F = \int_0^L (dm)\omega^2 r = \frac{M}{L}\omega^2 \int_0^L r\,dr = \frac{1}{2}M\omega^2 L$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.
